Mixture cure models

Source: R/operators2.R
cure.Rd

A fraction cure of subjects never has the event: S(t) = cure + (1 - cure) S0(t) and f(t) = (1 - cure) f0(t) (Boag 1949; Berkson and Gage 1952; Farewell 1982). The cure fraction is a parameter in (0, 1) with a logit link, so cure ~ z gives the incidence model and the base parameters give the latency model. Use with right censored responses (surv()); the law is improper (its distribution function tends to 1 - cure).

Usage

cure(base)

Arguments

base

A family for the event time of uncured subjects.

Value

A regcomp_family.

Examples

cw <- cure("weibull")
set.seed(1)
n <- 400; cured <- runif(n) < 0.3
t <- ifelse(cured, Inf, rweibull(n, 1.5, 2)); cens <- runif(n, 0, 6)
d <- data.frame(time = pmin(t, cens), event = as.numeric(t <= cens))
fit <- regcomp(surv(time, event) ~ 1, family = cw, data = d)
plogis(coef(fit)["cure:(Intercept)"])
#> cure:(Intercept) 
#>        0.2884821
